turns.doctor_question: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: Nice to meet you too. I came in because... well, since I started helping with the safety trainings at work, I just can’t seem to stop noticing how wrinkly and uneven my hands look when I’m pointing things out to people. It's really bothering me. And then, from there, I start thinking my face looks crooked in the newsletter photos. I mean, other people say they don’t see it at all when I bring it up, but I just can't stop focusing on it.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes persistent, distressing focus on perceived defects in their appearance (wrinkly, uneven hands and a crooked face) that others report not seeing.

turns.doctor_question: Do you repeatedly check your hands or face in mirrors, photos, or other reflective surfaces?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I do. Before I have to do a class, or... well, even before a senior-center workshop I go to, I’ll usually check the bathroom mirror a few times. I make sure to put lotion on my hands, and I'll turn my face different ways in the glass just to see how it looks. Sometimes I'll even ask a coworker if I look all right. Doing all that makes me run a little behind sometimes, but I still get myself there.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient explicitly confirms engaging in appearance-related repetitive behaviors, including checking mirrors repeatedly, inspecting their face from different angles, and seeking reassurance from coworkers.

turns.doctor_question: When you feel compelled to check your hands or face, what specific thought about your appearance is troubling you?
turns.patient_response:
Well, it's mostly what I was saying when I first came in. The main thing going through my head is just how wrinkly and uneven my hands are going to look to everyone when I'm up there pointing at the safety charts. 

And with my face, I just keep thinking about how crooked it looks, like how I saw it in those newsletter photos. Even though my coworkers tell me they don't see what I'm talking about at all, those thoughts just get stuck in my head, and I feel like I need to look just to be sure.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes persistent preoccupation with perceived flaws in their hands (wrinkly and uneven) and face (crooked), which coworkers explicitly do not observe.
symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient reports feeling driven to look and check their appearance 'just to be sure' in response to their appearance-related thoughts.
